profile.entities: Jubilant FoodWorks Ltd; Domino's Pizza India; Popeyes; Hong's; Dunkin'
profile.subseg: Pizza; Delivery; Dine-in; Takeaway; Premium Products
profile.themes: Margin Pressure from Energy & Labor Inflation; Market Share Gains in Pizza; Store Format Optimization; Premium Product Mix Shift

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing growth capex (store expansion); debt reduction (net debt down Rs. 200 Cr YoY); reinvestment in premium product R&D and delivery fleet electrification; no dividend increase planned in FY27
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Sustained LPG price volatility; wage inflation across 11+ states; delivery mix increasing labor cost burden; competitive discounting from Domino's; consumer sensitivity to price hikes; supply chain disruption from geopolitical events
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term growth (5-7% LFL) and margin recovery (200 bps over 2 years); transparent on near-term headwinds; focused on volume over short-term margin; proactive on cost control, electrification, and premiumization; dismissive of short-term noise
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Electric delivery fleet now covers majority of operations, reducing LPG exposure; internal R&D kits for oven conversion have cut capex and improved operational resilience; premium product mix (Sourdough, Big Big Pizza) is driving margin expansion despite lower average ticket size
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Pizza: 85% of revenue; Delivery: 76% of sales (up from 72% YoY); Dine-in: low base, decelerated growth; Premium products (Big Big Pizza, Sourdough): 15% of sales, 300 bps higher margin; Dunkin': losses narrowing; Popeyes/Hong's: dilutive but under control
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LPG price volatility and labor cost inflation | Zomato | loser | High | Zomato lacks owned delivery fleet and is more exposed to third-party delivery cost inflation; Jubilant's owned electric fleet provides structural advantage |
| Need for premium product innovation and margin expansion | Haldiram's | beneficiary | Med | Jubilant's premium pizza mix and operational efficiency may pressure Haldiram's QSR positioning in premium snack segment |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin: 75.5% (up 100 bps YoY) driven by waste reduction, premium mix, calibrated pricing; EBITDA margin: pressured by 120 bps energy cost inflation (LPG/PNG), 50-60 bps labor inflation (minimum wage hikes + delivery mix), and 20-30 bps commodity inflation; net margin compression expected in FY27Q1-Q2
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 5-7% LFL annual; margin: 200 bps expansion over 2 years; order inflow: N/A; capex/commissioning: Rs. 1,800-2,000 Cr for 230-250 new stores (capex/store down 20% YoY for 3 years)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into Tier 3/4 cities with smaller 600-700 sq ft delivery-focused stores; potential for Dunkin' profitability by FY28; untapped premium product penetration; delivery fleet electrification scale-up
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Jubilant FoodWorks gained pizza market share despite Q4 LFL growth deceleration to 0.2%, driven by conscious reduction in minimum order value to Rs.99 and premium product launches; near-term margin compression from 120 bps energy inflation and labor cost hikes is expected, but structural improvements in gross margin and capex efficiency support 200 bps margin expansion target over two years.
